reason: Internal: design bundle only, no code. The evaluation bundle is corrected to record that the evaluation SDK it was supposed to be built on is never mentioned anywhere in it. A grep for strands_evals across all 1,601 lines of design/evaluation/ returns zero hits, so strands-agents-evals — pinned at pyproject.toml:47 the whole time — was never adopted, never rejected and never reasoned about across seven nodes. That is a different failure from deciding wrongly: there is no argument to attack, so nothing in the bundle could have caught it. The operator's locked decision predates the bundle and the OLD layer never implemented it either; its two SDK classes were defined and no call site anywhere in the tree ever instantiated them, which their own docstring stated. Three of the four primitives 01-boundaries section 2 derives from first principles already ship — Case, Experiment.run_evaluations, and EvaluationData with EvaluationOutput — which is 1,037 of the rebuilt layer's 2,267 lines; the SUBJECT is the one that is genuinely ours and is what the bundle actually found. Two blocking reasons were checked against the installed package and are false: a task function may return a plain dict, so the subject need not be a Strands Agent, and judge-based evaluators take a model argument typed Model or str, so OpenAIModel against OmniRoute works exactly as production already does it at nora/agent/factory.py:128. Two new nodes carry the investigation — 07-sdk-native.md for the correction and 08-the-sdk-surface.md for the subsystem inventory — and seven files are edited, with _index.yaml dropping from implemented to checkpoint. FOUR CLAIMS ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE. The routing tier was recorded in 04-the-convention section 6, GOAL.md step 8 and _index.yaml as unrecoverable when the SDK ships four instruments for it. GOAL.md step 5 was reported done when no decision was ever recorded, because two different step fives exist in one bundle and one of them is the delete. 00-overview section 3 still carried the sentence about there being no target shape, which _index.yaml had already retracted in its own copy but not in the source. And the claim that 21 proactive plus 2 participation cases are refused for missing seams is RETRACTED: both seams were closed two commits earlier, 22 proactive cases ran in the last live run, and the remaining guard cannot fire at all because the 11 cases carrying its trigger enter at a different entry point than the one holding it. THE DEEPER READ, and it is where three adversarial reviews landed hardest: the first draft of 08 was written off documentation with a shallow probe and was wrong in both directions. TracedHandler already ships the span-to-Session seam it filed as the highest-value work. The relevance gate's 40 cases are not an open risk but a measured break — Nora emits zero span events repo-wide, so the mapper produces an empty Session, the evaluator raises, and the SDK scores the case zero silently. ERROR collapses into FAIL below any grader we can write, because Experiment._worker writes test_pass false without calling a single evaluator and the report has no error channel. The eval_task wrapper is synchronous and never awaits, while all five entry points are async. Sampling has no SDK counterpart and is mutually exclusive with the result cache. StateEquals expresses one of four assertions and must_cite is structurally impossible. And eight further responsibilities — clock injection, database lifecycle, room isolation, async teardown, DSN scrubbing, compose-failure separation, judging against live doctrine, per-entry-point config — belong to us and to no SDK. The conclusion survived all three reviews: the harness was never the part that needed writing, it is the part that was written. The price of the seam is what moved. LIMITS: nothing has been run; both new nodes name the run that would refute them; red teaming is experimental and its TargetSession seam is unprobed, so the five injection corpora are not safe to retire; skill-level evaluators need 1.2.0; and PR #334 is held rather than merged or closed, because nora/subject/ and the thirteen corpora are the base any replacement builds on. Nothing a member of a room can observe.
